content:
The image displays a mango leaf with dark, superficial fungal deposits covering a significant portion of its surface. The underlying leaf tissue appears to be green, consistent with the description of Sooty Mould, where the fungus grows on honeydew secreted by insects rather than infecting the leaf itself. The dark, soot-like appearance matches the primary symptom of Sooty Mould. There are no signs of small, black, irregular spots expanding into dead areas (Anthracnose) or leaf rolling and twig dieback (Die_Back). The symptoms do not resemble a powdery white substance, ruling out Powdery Mildew.
